name: SEESARE cycle-block study on a cent account (Tokyo fix through the real ledger rules)
source: study: research/seesare/cycle_study.py (design committed before results) -> research/results/seesare/cycle_study.json
hypothesis: Owner's Phase 3 directive: on a RoboForex ProCent (cent) account every SEESARE level can place real micro-orders, multi-leg cycles give +2% or more per 10-event cycle, and the drawdown stays inside the 3.6% box over 5-10 cycle sequences in every era 2011-2025.
verdict: Rejected as stated: the box holds (max drawdown 0.005-0.016%) only because real trading almost stops. With losing time exits NEGATIVE (hardcoded) and no target, the ladder can only descend: L15 from event 13, 98.8% of 1,071 events there, 6 REAL trades in 15 years (-$0.04), 0 cycles closed. Target at 1.04: same 6 REAL. Time exits MANUAL: 25 REAL, 2 cycles (+0.003%, +0.116%). The cent account makes the Tokyo fix REAL only at L0-L3 (ratio 1.04), L0-L9 at 3.5. +2% per cycle needs +1.46R per event at L0 (mult 1.0); the Tokyo fix earns about +0.05R.

name: SEESARE time-exit ascension study (Tokyo fix, cent account)
hypothesis: Owner's Phase 4 directive: counting winning time exits as positive (climb one level) un-freezes the SEESARE ladder so the Tokyo fix trades real cent lots, and a ladder scaled to the owner's -0.35% L0 loss (4:1 spec) gives cycle momentum inside the 3.6% envelope.
verdict: Rejected: the ladder still sinks. The flow wins 52.6% of mornings after the 1.9-pip spread (49.3% at 2.85); with +1 up and -2/-3/-4 down the ladder settles near L13 (mean level 13.1-13.9, L0 0.1-0.5% of mornings). Real trades in 15 years: 15 (default ladder), 22 (owner-scaled), 191 (owner-scaled and declared 4:1, which the flow does not have). Cycles closed 1/2/19; best variant's cycles: mean +0.021%, median -0.003%, 26% positive; at 2.85 pips -0.018% mean, 8% positive. Max drawdown 0.005-0.24%, guard never needed. Arithmetic: the ladder needs about a 75% win rate to spend half its time in L0-L3.
